status: ROOT_FROZEN implementation authorized NOW (parallel with I01-B6-C and all Wave-1 packets)
scope: Only the mandatory close/init worker-lock race fix in sogni-provider.ts plus coverage tests. No composer, wiring, routes, scripts, or contract changes.
dependency: Base 21e1e7a (zcode/production-core). Disjoint from I01-B6-C owns (verified). Source of the mandate: reports/I01-B6-P-integrated.json mandatoryFollowup.
defect: getClient attempt catch (sogni-provider.ts:181) runs releaseOwnership() only when epoch===attemptEpoch. Sequence: worker-role attempt A starts (epoch 0) and pauses before lock acquisition; close() bumps epoch to 1 and its cleanup releases (no-op) and finishes; A resumes, acquires lockServer+lockHandle, createInstance resolves, epoch check fails, A disposes its client and throws WITHOUT releasing — the just-acquired worker socket/pid lock is orphaned until process exit; next worker init fails 'Another local worker owns the Sogni worker app ID'.
fixProtocol: Track ownership per attempt: add a transport-scoped lockOwnerEpoch (number|null, initially null). The worker-role branch sets lockOwnerEpoch=attemptEpoch immediately after BOTH acquireWorkerSocket and acquireWorkerPidFile succeed. releaseOwnership() clears it to null when it releases.

In the attempt catch, release when this attempt still owns the locks regardless of epoch: if lockOwnerEpoch===attemptEpoch => await releaseOwnership() (which sets null), in addition to the existing epoch===attemptEpoch cleanup. A newer live attempt's locks are never released by a stale attempt (their epochs differ).
close()'s cleanup releaseOwnership() must be a no-op when lockOwnerEpoch===null (another owner/no owner) so a post-close racing attempt that acquires later keeps its own cleanup responsibility.

Do not change: post-close submit denial (the ERR_INVALID_STATE fix), observeAccount/subscription whitelist, guard ordering, app-ID persistence, or any test fixture semantics. Behavior-preserving refactor only within createSogniSdkTransport.
